content.summary: The framing correctly separates a finite support reduction, a paper proof of the stronger support bound, and a near-extremal completion argument from any actual exclusion of the rank-four obstruction. The explicit distinct-member and empty-core conventions avoid two common sunflower ambiguities. The reflexive intersection convention also makes the rank-zero endpoint coherent. I verified the general inequality's stated interface and elementary counting argument; I have not yet certified the complete support-56 or nine-triple arguments in this framing round. The manuscript's distinction between local unresolved Lean inputs and a previously reported computational extremal result is mathematically appropriate, subject to the scheduled source audit.

checks.method: Read the snapshot, contract, manuscript and E01; recomputed the canonical snapshot-object digest and manuscript byte digest, then compared the prose hypotheses to the source theorem parameters.
checks.observation: Both digests match their declared values. E01 quantifies arbitrary Type u, finite distinct sets, uniformity, reflexive nonempty intersections and a global point-degree bound. The prose accurately reflects this interface. A singleton family containing the empty set fails reflexive intersection, so rank zero forces the empty family.

checks.method: Independently reconstructed the two incidence sums and checked exact equality examples in Python for a triangle of pairs and a three-petal star. Inspected the subset-selection and relabeling steps in E01.
checks.observation: The per-point upper bound is equivalent to (d-1)(D-d)>=0. The examples give 18=18 and 24=24 respectively; the sunflower star confirms that the general theorem needs no sunflower-free premise. Substituting m=28,r=4,D=19 gives 19n<=1372 and n<=72. Selecting exactly 28 members preserves the hypotheses, and injective support relabeling yields an obstruction predicate without proving its nonexistence.
